segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So, hello everyone.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: My name’s Lou Miller and I’m going to be your tour guide today as we take this fantastic boat trip around the Tasmanian coast.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Before we set off, I just want to tell you a few things about our journey.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Our boats aren’t huge as you can see.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We already have three staff members on board and on top of that, we can transport a further fifteen people - that’s you - around the coastline.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But please note if there are more than nine people on either side of the boat, we’ll move some of you over, otherwise all eighteen of us will end up in the sea!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’ve recently upgraded all our boats.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They used to be jet black, but our new ones now have these comfortable dark red seats and a light-green exterior in order to stand out from others and help promote our company.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This gives our boats a rather unique appearance, don’t you think?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We offer you a free lunchbox during the trip and we have three types.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Lunchbox 1 contains ham and tomato sandwiches.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Lunchbox 2 contains a Cheddar cheese roll and Lunchbox 3 is salad-based and also contains eggs and tuna.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: All three lunchboxes also have a packet of crisps and chocolate bar inside.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Please let staff know which lunchbox you prefer.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I'm sure I don't have to ask you not to throw anything into the sea.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We don't have any bins to put litter in, but Jess, myself or Ray, our other guide, will collect it from you after lunch and put it all in a large plastic sack.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The engine on the boat makes quite a lot of noise so before we head off, let me tell you a few things about what you’re going to see.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This area is famous for its ancient lighthouse, which you'll see from the boat as we turn past the first little island.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It was built in 1838 to protect sailors as a number of shipwrecks had /16 led to significant loss of life.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The construction itself was complicated as some of the original drawings kept by the local council show.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It sits right on top of the cliffs in a very isolated spot.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In the nineteenth century there were many jobs there, such as polishing the brass lamps, chopping firewood and cleaning windows, that kept lighthouse keepers busy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: These workers were mainly prison convicts until the middle of that century when ordinary families willing to /16 live in such circumstances took over.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Some of you have asked me what creatures we can expect to see.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I know everyone loves the penguins, but they're very shy and, unfortunately, tend to hide from passing boats, but you might see birds in the distance, such as sea eagles, flying around the cliff edges where they nest.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When we get to the rocky area inhabited by fur seals, we'll stop and watch them /18 swimming around the coast.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They’re inquisitive creatures so don’t be surprised if one pops up right in front of you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Their predators, orca whales, hunt along the coastline too, but spotting one of these is rare.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Dolphins, on the other hand, can sometimes approach on their own or in /18 groups as they ride the waves beside us.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Lastly, I want to mention the caves.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Tasmania is famous for its caves and the ones we'll pass by are so amazing that people are lost for words when they see them.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They can only /20 be approached by sea, but if you feel that you want to see more than we’re able to show you, then you can take a kayak into the area on another day and one of our staff will give you more information on that.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: What we’ll do is to go through a narrow channel, past some incredible rock formations and from there we’ll be able to see the openings to the caves, and /20 at that point we’ll talk to you about what lies beyond.
